facts.f: Carbohydrates give us energy.
facts.e: Rice, wheat, millets and potatoes are rich in carbohydrates.

facts.f: Proteins help the body grow and repair itself.
facts.e: Dal, eggs, milk, paneer, beans and nuts are good sources of protein.

facts.f: Fats give the body energy and help keep it warm.
facts.e: We need some fat, like ghee, oil and nuts, but too much is unhealthy.

facts.f: Vitamin C helps the body heal wounds and fight infections.
facts.e: Citrus fruits like oranges and lemons, and amla, are rich in vitamin C.

facts.f: Amla, the Indian gooseberry, is one of the richest sources of vitamin C.
facts.e: It is sour and is often eaten as a pickle, juice or murabba.

facts.f: Vitamin A is important for good eyesight.
facts.e: Carrots, papaya, mangoes and green leafy vegetables help the body get vitamin A.

facts.f: Iron helps the body make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood.
facts.e: Too little iron can cause anaemia, which makes people tired and pale. Spinach, jaggery and pulses contain iron.

facts.f: Iodine in salt helps prevent goitre, a swelling in the neck.
facts.e: The thyroid gland needs iodine to work properly. That is why salt in India is iodised.

facts.f: Fibre in food helps digestion.
facts.e: Whole grains, fruits, vegetables and pulses are full of fibre.

facts.f: Our body needs water every day.
facts.e: Water helps carry nutrients, control body temperature and remove waste.

facts.f: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts.
facts.e: That means carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.

facts.f: Turmeric gets its yellow colour from a substance called curcumin.
facts.e: Turmeric is used in almost every Indian kitchen.

facts.f: Sealed honey can stay good to eat for a very long time.
facts.e: It has very little water and is slightly acidic, so germs find it hard to grow.

facts.f: Tomatoes, potatoes and chillies came to India from the Americas.
facts.e: European traders, mainly the Portuguese, brought them to India in the 1500s and 1600s.

facts.f: Tea first became popular in China. Today Assam and Darjeeling teas are famous worldwide.
facts.e: India is one of the world's biggest tea producers.

facts.f: A tomato is a fruit, scientifically speaking.
facts.e: Botanists call any part of a plant that grows from a flower and holds seeds a fruit.

facts.f: Bananas are berries, scientifically speaking, but strawberries are not.
facts.e: Botanists have special rules for what counts as a berry.

facts.f: Peanuts are not true nuts. They are legumes, like peas and beans.
facts.e: Peanuts grow underground in pods.

facts.f: Millets like ragi, jowar and bajra are very nutritious grains.
facts.e: The United Nations named 2023 the International Year of Millets, after India proposed it.

facts.f: Brushing your teeth twice a day helps prevent cavities.
facts.e: Brush in the morning and before bed.

facts.f: Children aged 6 to 12 need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep each night.
facts.e: Sleep helps the body grow and the brain learn.

facts.f: Children should be active for at least 60 minutes a day, on average.
facts.e: This is the advice of the World Health Organization. Playing, running and cycling all count.

facts.f: Wash fruits and vegetables before eating them.
facts.e: Washing removes dirt and germs.

facts.f: Eating too many sweets can cause tooth decay.
facts.e: Germs in the mouth turn sugar into acid that damages teeth.

facts.f: Idli and dosa batter rises because of fermentation.
facts.e: Tiny microbes in the batter feed on it and make gas bubbles.

facts.f: Curd is made when helpful bacteria turn milk thick and sour.
facts.e: A spoon of old curd added to warm milk starts the process.

facts.f: India is the world's largest producer of spices.
facts.e: India grows many spices, including turmeric, chilli, cumin, cardamom and black pepper.

facts.f: Black pepper is native to the Western Ghats of India.
facts.e: It was so valuable in ancient trade that it was called 'black gold'.

facts.f: Saffron is the most expensive spice in the world by weight.
facts.e: It comes from tiny threads inside crocus flowers, picked by hand. In India it is grown in Kashmir.

facts.f: Rice is a main food for more than half of the world's people.
facts.e: India and China grow more rice than any other countries.

facts.f: Junk food usually has too much salt, sugar or fat.
facts.e: It is fine as a treat, but not as everyday food.

facts.f: Cholera spreads through dirty water and food.
facts.e: Boiling or filtering water and washing hands help prevent it.

facts.f: Malaria and dengue are spread by mosquito bites.
facts.e: Not letting water stand in coolers, pots and tyres stops mosquitoes from breeding.

facts.f: Cooking food properly kills many germs.
facts.e: Keep cooked food covered so flies cannot sit on it.

facts.f: Some people are allergic to foods like peanuts, milk or eggs.
facts.e: An allergy means the body reacts to something that is harmless to most people.

facts.f: India grows more mangoes than any other country.
facts.e: There are hundreds of varieties, like Alphonso, Dasheri and Langra.

facts.f: Eating too much salt can raise blood pressure.
facts.e: It is healthier to keep salt and salty snacks in check.

facts.f: Eat a rainbow: different coloured fruits and vegetables give different nutrients.
facts.e: Try to have something green, orange, red and purple each week.

facts.f: Chocolate is made from the seeds of the cacao tree.
facts.e: The seeds, called cocoa beans, are fermented, dried and roasted.

facts.f: In 1747, ship's doctor James Lind found that citrus fruits cured scurvy.
facts.e: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C. Sailors on long voyages often suffered from it.

facts.f: Ragi (finger millet) is very rich in calcium.
facts.e: Ragi porridge and rotis are popular in Karnataka and other states.

facts.f: Cucumbers and watermelons are more than 90% water.
facts.e: They are great for staying cool on hot days.

quiz.q: Which nutrient mainly gives us energy?
quiz.x: Rice, wheat and potatoes are full of carbohydrates.

quiz.q: Which nutrient helps the body grow and repair itself?
quiz.x: Dal, eggs and paneer are rich in protein.

quiz.q: A lack of iodine can cause which problem?
quiz.x: That is why salt is iodised.

quiz.q: A lack of vitamin C causes which disease?
quiz.x: Citrus fruits and amla prevent scurvy.

quiz.q: Which of these is very rich in vitamin C?
quiz.x: Amla, the Indian gooseberry, is packed with vitamin C.

quiz.q: What gives turmeric its yellow colour?
quiz.x: Capsaicin is what makes chillies hot.

quiz.q: Which of these is a millet?
quiz.x: Ragi, jowar and bajra are millets.

quiz.q: Which year did the UN name the International Year of Millets?
quiz.x: India proposed it, and the UN named 2023 the Year of Millets.

quiz.q: Which is the most expensive spice by weight?
quiz.x: Saffron threads are picked by hand from crocus flowers.

quiz.q: What turns milk into curd?
quiz.x: Bacteria in a little old curd turn warm milk into curd.

quiz.q: Scientifically, what are peanuts?
quiz.x: Peanuts grow in pods underground, like peas and beans.

quiz.q: Which of these came to India from the Americas?
quiz.x: Portuguese traders brought chillies about 500 years ago.

quiz.q: How often should you brush your teeth?
quiz.x: Brush in the morning and before bed.

quiz.q: How long should children be active every day, according to the WHO?
quiz.x: The WHO advises an average of at least 60 minutes a day. Running, playing and cycling all count.

quiz.q: How does cholera usually spread?
quiz.x: Clean water and handwashing prevent cholera.

quiz.q: What spreads dengue?
quiz.x: Dengue spreads through the bite of certain mosquitoes.

quiz.q: Which vitamin is especially important for good eyesight?
quiz.x: Carrots and papaya help the body get vitamin A.

quiz.q: Which of these is a fruit, scientifically speaking?
quiz.x: Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds.

quiz.q: A lack of iron can cause which problem?
quiz.x: Iron helps the blood carry oxygen.

quiz.q: Chocolate is made from...
quiz.x: Cacao seeds are also called cocoa beans.

quiz.q: What is a balanced diet?
o: All nutrients in the right amounts
quiz.x: A balanced diet includes many kinds of food.

quiz.q: Which country grows the most mangoes?
quiz.x: India grows more mangoes than any other country.
